patient.history_present_illness:
Ms. Eleanor Voss is a 71-year-old right-handed retired school librarian presenting to the neurology outpatient clinic with her husband, Richard, for evaluation of a progressive left hand tremor and generalized slowing over the past two years. She first noticed a subtle intermittent shaking in her left hand approximately two and a half years ago while seated reading in the evenings. She initially attributed the tremor to fatigue or stress, and a neighbor suggested it might be 'the same tremor that runs in the family', since her mother had had shaky hands for many years and was never formally diagnosed. Over the past 18 months the tremor became more persistent and obvious, particularly when her hands were resting in her lap or on the armrests of a chair. Her husband first noticed it clearly during a church service when her left hand was trembling on her knee. Importantly, she notes the shaking virtually disappears when she reaches for objects or is using her hand purposefully, and returns once the hand is again at rest. She has not noticed that the tremor responds to alcohol.

Over the past year she has developed progressive slowing of her left hand in daily tasks. Fastening buttons on her blouse with her left hand has become difficult, she has stopped using left-handed scissors, and her handwriting has become progressively smaller and harder to read. Her husband has noticed she takes noticeably longer to get ready in the morning and that her left arm does not swing when she walks. She describes a pervasive stiffness in the left arm and shoulder, initially attributed to arthritis, but persistent despite conservative measures. Over the past six months she has noticed a change in her gait: shorter steps and a slight forward lean. She has not fallen but felt unsteady turning quickly in the kitchen on one occasion three months ago. Her voice has become softer and her husband frequently asks her to repeat herself. She has also noticed progressive difficulty with her sense of smell for approximately two years, blaming sinus issues. Constipation has developed over the past 18 months, requiring a fiber supplement daily. She denies vivid dreams, acting out dreams, visual hallucinations, cognitive complaints, or urinary incontinence. Sleep is otherwise reportedly adequate. There are no symptoms suggestive of orthostatic lightheadedness, syncope, or cerebellar dysfunction. She is on no medications that could cause or worsen parkinsonism. She has severe longstanding claustrophobia and declined brain MRI despite preparation; she also declined sedation but agreed to non-contrast CT.

neurological_exam.additional: Myerson sign positive (fails to habituate after 10 glabellar taps). Handwriting sample shows progressive micrographia with diminishing letter size across a sentence. Seborrhea noted on nasolabial folds. Olfactory inquiry: patient acknowledges she has been unable to smell her perfume for approximately 2 years; she attributed it to 'sinus problems.'
neurological_exam.coordination: Finger-to-nose without dysmetria bilaterally, though left-hand movements are slow. Heel-to-shin intact. Rapid alternating movements markedly slow and decremental on the left, mildly slow on the right. No intention tremor.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Pupils equal, round, and reactive to light bilaterally. Extraocular movements full; no nystagmus. Blink rate reduced. Facial expression mildly hypomimic bilaterally, more prominent on the left. Facial sensation intact. Hearing grossly intact. Palate elevates symmetrically. Tongue midline without fasciculations. Shoulder shrug 5/5 bilaterally.
neurological_exam.gait: Mildly stooped posture. Reduced left arm swing during ambulation. Stride length mildly shortened, left lower extremity step slightly shorter than right. Gait initiation mildly hesitant. No festination observed. En bloc turns requiring 4-5 steps. Pull test: one step of retropulsion, self-corrected, no fall. Romberg sign negative.
neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert and fully oriented to person, place, time, and situation. Speech mildly hypophonic but fluent with intact comprehension and repetition. Naming intact. MoCA 28/30 (lost 1 point on letter fluency, 1 point on serial sevens). Affect mildly flat but appropriately engaged and interactive.
neurological_exam.motor: Tone: Cogwheel rigidity at the left wrist and left elbow, accentuated with contralateral activation maneuver (right fist clenching). Mild rigidity at the left ankle. Right upper extremity tone normal. Strength 5/5 throughout all four extremities. Bradykinesia prominent in the left upper extremity: reduced speed and amplitude on finger tapping (left > right), hand opening/closing, and pronation-supination. Mild bradykinesia in the right upper extremity. Left hand rest tremor at 4-5 Hz, pill-rolling in character, present at rest and with arm fully supported in the lap, suppressed transiently with voluntary movement and re-emerging on repositioning. No tremor in the right hand or lower extremities during rest. Mild postural tremor left hand with outstretched arms.
neurological_exam.reflexes: 2+ and symmetric at biceps, triceps, brachioradialis, patellar, and Achilles tendons bilaterally. Plantar responses flexor bilaterally. No Hoffmann sign.
neurological_exam.sensory: Light touch, pinprick, proprioception, and vibration intact throughout all extremities. No cortical sensory deficits.
